title.value: Decomposing the Brain in Autism: Linking Behavioral Domains to Neuroanatomical Variation and Genomic Underpinnings
title.justification: The title of the paper is mentioned at the beginning of the document, indicating the study's focus on autism and its correlation with neuroanatomical and genomic factors.
title.quote: Decomposing the Brain in Autism: Linking Behavioral Domains to Neuroanatomical Variation and Genomic Underpinnings

analysis.description: This study examines the variability in brain anatomy associated with autism using a dimensional approach to assess correlations with behavioral domains such as social communication, interaction, and sensory processing. It involves a large sample from the EU-AIMS LEAP project and integrates neuroimaging data with genomic data to better understand the molecular underpinnings of autism.

type.justification: The study involves analyses and experiments on neuroimaging and genomic data of autistic individuals to identify correlations with behavioral domains, making it empirical.
type.quote: We examined interindividual neuroanatomical differences using a dimensional approach... correlated with cortical gene expression profiles via the Allen Human Brain Atlas.

name.justification: The research primarily uses neuroimaging techniques to correlate brain structure with behavioral and genomic data in autism.
name.quote: To elucidate the neuroanatomical underpinnings of autism, most structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) studies have employed...

name.quote: These domain-specific imaging patterns were enriched for genes that... are differentially expressed in autism.

name.justification: The study explores autism-related symptoms and traits and their neuroanatomical and genomic associations.
name.quote: Autism is accompanied by highly individualized patterns of neurodevelopmental differences in brain anatomy.
